manage.accounts.logout_confirm.descripti: Installed games stay on disk. To install, update or launch online games from this store you need to log in again.
manage.accounts.account_expired: Log in again to use this account
manage.accounts.signed_out_installed_one: Logged out · 1 game installed with it
manage.accounts.signed_out_installed_oth: Logged out · {count} games installed with it

manage.steam_library.hint: Without a sign-in, Irori can read every game you own from the Steam client on this computer.
manage.steam_library.waiting: Turned on. Irori reads your Steam library once Steam has restarted.
manage.steam_library.games_one: 1 game read from the Steam client {when}.
manage.steam_library.games_other: {count} games read from the Steam client {when}.
manage.steam_library.kept_on: Remote debugging stays on, and Irori reads your library again while Steam runs.
manage.steam_library.other_program: Another program turned on Steam’s remote debugging. Irori leaves it as it is.
manage.steam_library.dialog.title: Read your library from Steam
manage.steam_library.dialog.what: Irori can list every game of your Steam library, installed or not, without a Steam sign-in in Irori. It reads them from the Steam client on this computer and sends them nowhere.
manage.steam_library.dialog.how: For that, Irori creates the file .cef-enable-remote-debugging in Steam’s folder. Steam reads it when it starts, so Steam has to restart. Irori asks before restarting it.
manage.steam_library.dialog.risk: While it’s on, any program on this computer can control the Steam client through a local port.
manage.steam_library.dialog.once: Read once and switch it off again
manage.steam_library.dialog.once_help: Irori removes the file after reading. Steam closes the port the next time it starts.
manage.steam_library.dialog.keep_help: The file stays, and Irori reads your library again whenever it refreshes while Steam runs.
manage.steam_library.restart.title: Restart Steam?
manage.steam_library.restart.description: Steam has to start again to turn on remote debugging. Games running in Steam close with it.
manage.steam_library.read_failed: Couldn’t read your library from Steam
manage.steam_library.switched_off: Switched off. Steam closes its debugging port the next time it starts.
manage.steam_library.switch_off_failed: Couldn’t switch off Steam’s remote debugging
manage.steam_library.forget_failed: Couldn’t remove the games read from Steam
manage.steam_library.error.not_running: Steam isn’t running. Start Steam and try again.
manage.steam_library.error.debugging_off: Steam runs without remote debugging. Restart Steam to turn it on.
manage.steam_library.error.millennium: Irori can’t find Steam’s debugging port. Millennium manages that port; check Millennium’s settings.
manage.steam_library.error.not_steam: Another program uses port {port}, which Steam’s remote debugging needs.
manage.steam_library.sign_in_instead.des: Restarting Steam won’t free that port. Connect your Steam account in Irori instead (through Steam’s official web sign-in or a Web API key), and Irori lists every game you own without the debugging port.
manage.steam_library.error.starting: Steam hasn’t loaded your library yet. Sign in to Steam, wait for your library to show and try again.
manage.steam_library.error.unsupported: This version of Steam keeps its library where Irori can’t read it.
manage.steam_library.error.session: Steam runs this session, so Irori can’t restart it.
manage.steam_hidden.count_one: 1 game you hid in Steam is hidden here too.
manage.steam_hidden.count_other: {count} games you hid in Steam are hidden here too.
manage.steam_hidden.unknown_account: Irori can’t see which games you hid in Steam: Steam on this computer keeps no library data for this account. Sign in to it in Steam once, and Irori sees them at its next library refresh.
manage.steam_hidden.unknown_local: Irori can’t see which games you hid in Steam: Steam on this computer keeps no library data Irori can read.
manage.accounts.optional_logout_descript: Installed {store} games stay in your library. Games you haven’t installed leave it until you log in again.
manage.accounts.expired_banner: Login expired for {stores}. Log in again below to refresh your library.
manage.accounts.hide_tooltip: Hides this store and its games from your library. Your sign-in and installed games stay intact.
manage.accounts.rescan_tooltip: Checks your computer again for installed games on disk. Works offline.
manage.accounts.steam_account_tip: Connect via Steam’s official sign-in window or a Web API key to add owned games you haven’t installed, playtime, friends, and achievements.
manage.steam_library.section_tip: Reads every owned game directly from your local Steam client without signing in to Steam inside Irori.

manage.news.no_match: No posts match the current filters.

manage.deals.shown_notice: Store deals show on the Stores page again.
manage.deals.hidden_notice: Store deals are hidden. Show them again in Settings → General.

manage.downloads.stop_update.title: Stop updating “{title}”?
manage.downloads.stop_update.description: The installed version stays playable. You can update later.
manage.downloads.history.title: History
manage.downloads.pill.title: Downloads
manage.downloads.command.keep_on: Keep the computer on after the downloads
manage.downloads.command.screen_off: Turn the screen off while downloading

manage.downloads.screen_off_failed: The screen couldn’t be turned off

manage.login.another_in_browser: If the page signs you in to an account that’s already here, log out on the {store} website first, then sign in with the other account.
manage.login.input_placeholder: Paste the code or address here
manage.login.step.sign_in: Sign in on the store’s website
manage.login.step.opened: The sign-in page opened in your browser.
manage.login.auto_detect: Irori signs in as soon as you copy it.
manage.login.window.waiting: Sign in in the window that opened. Irori finishes as soon as {store} confirms it.
manage.login.window.missing: Irori's sign-in window isn't installed, so the page opened in your browser.
manage.login.window.failed: The sign-in window couldn't open, so the page opened in your browser.
manage.steam.intro: Installed Steam games already work without connecting. Choose one of the two ways below to add your full library, playtime, friends and achievements.
manage.steam.web.summary: Opens Steam’s official sign-in page in Irori’s sign-in window. You can use the Steam Mobile QR code or Steam Guard; Irori never sees your password. Supports private profiles and Steam Family.
manage.steam.web.vpn_notice: Avoid signing in through a VPN if possible, because Steam may flag logins from unfamiliar locations. If you use a VPN, the Steam Web API key tab creates no login session at all.
manage.steam.web.waiting: Sign in on Steam’s page in the window that opened. Irori finishes as soon as Steam completes the login.
manage.steam.web.closed: The Steam sign-in window was closed before finishing.
manage.steam.web.no_window: Irori’s sign-in window isn’t installed in this build. Use a Steam Web API key instead.
manage.steam.api.summary: Connects with your personal Steam Web API key instead of signing in. No Steam login session is created, it never expires, and it works behind VPNs. Requires public Game Details and does not include Steam Family.
manage.steam.api.step1_title: Get your Steam Web API key
manage.steam.api.step1_body: Open Steam’s API key page, enter any domain name (for example, localhost), and copy the 32-character key.
manage.steam.api.step2_body: Steam only shares your library with an API key when your profile’s Game Details setting is set to Public.
manage.steam.api.step3_title: Enter your SteamID64 and API key
manage.steam.api.steamid_detected: Detected from Steam on this computer.
manage.steam.api.error_steamid: Enter a valid 17-digit SteamID64 or a steamcommunity.com/profiles/… link.
manage.steam.api.error_key: Steam Web API keys are 32 hexadecimal characters (0-9, A-F).
manage.updates.components_note: Installs side by side — games keep their current version.
manage.updates.go_back_description: Restores the previous build and removes the current one. Games using {name} switch automatically.
manage.updates.go_back_failed: Couldn’t go back to the previous {name}

manage.updates.store_check_failed: Couldn’t reach {store} — showing last known updates
manage.updates.went_back: {name} is back on its previous build
manage.wine.title: Wine manager
manage.wine.description_macos: Download Wine builds for Windows games, or use an installed CrossOver or Whisky runtime.
manage.wine.description: Download Proton and Wine builds for Windows games, and see every build on this system.
manage.wine.description_running_one: Download Proton and Wine builds for Windows games. 1 install running.
manage.wine.description_running_other: Download Proton and Wine builds for Windows games. {count} installs running.
manage.wine.prefixes.empty.title: No Wine prefixes yet
manage.wine.prefixes.empty.description: A Windows game gets its prefix the first time it starts.
manage.wine.prefixes.hint: Each prefix is a Windows of its own. Only installed games count as using one.
manage.wine.prefixes.hint_unused: Each prefix is a Windows of its own. {count} aren’t used by an installed game; Storage can remove them.
manage.wine.prefixes.former: Not used by an installed game; it was the prefix of {games}
manage.wine.prefixes.unused: Not used by an installed game
manage.wine.prefixes.no_games: In use, by no installed game
manage.wine.source.ge_proton: Great all-round choice for most Windows games, with broad game fixes and extra video codecs.
manage.wine.source.proton_cachyos: Fast, gaming-tuned Proton with extra compatibility fixes and support for older DirectX and graphics cards.
manage.wine.source.proton_wineland: Experimental Proton focused on newer Wayland desktop features and smoother performance.
manage.wine.source.wine_ge: Older standalone Wine with game fixes. No longer updated; use GE-Proton or Proton-CachyOS instead.
manage.wine.source.wine_kron4ek: Standard Wine builds without Proton’s gaming layer, useful for classic Windows apps and troubleshooting.
manage.wine.source.nexus_runtime: Required for Microsoft Store and PC Game Pass games on Linux.
manage.wine.source.dw_proton: Community Proton with extra fixes for anime, gacha, and games that struggle on other builds. Downloaded from dawn.wine.
manage.wine.source.umu_proton: Minimal Proton close to Valve’s official Steam Proton, good as a clean baseline.
manage.wine.source.proton_em: Early-access Proton testing newer upscaling, HDR, and Wayland improvements. Builds marked TEST are experimental.
manage.wine.source.proton_sarek: Legacy Proton for older graphics cards. No longer updated; Proton-CachyOS now includes its fixes.
manage.wine.source.proton_ge_rtsp: GE-Proton with added RTSP video stream support, mainly useful for VRChat media players.
manage.wine.source.wine_crossover: Open-source Wine from CodeWeavers’ CrossOver project, well suited for Windows games and apps on macOS.
manage.wine.source.wine_staging_mac: Upstream Wine with experimental patches for macOS.
manage.wine.source.game_porting_toolkit: Apple’s translation layer for running DirectX 11 and 12 Windows games on Apple silicon Macs.
manage.wine.fetch_failed: Couldn’t fetch releases: {error}. GitHub may be limiting requests; try again later.
manage.wine.rate_limited: GitHub allows only a few release checks an hour without an account, and they are used up. Checks resume in {minutes} min.
manage.wine.remove_confirm.title: Remove {version}?
manage.wine.remove_confirm.default_descr: This is the default Wine for all games. Games without their own Wine setting will need another build before they can start.
manage.wine.remove_confirm.description: Games set to use this build will need another Wine or Proton build. You can download it again at any time.
manage.wine.empty.title: No versions found
manage.wine.empty.description: Refresh to fetch the release list again.
manage.wine.system.empty.title: No Wine or Proton found
manage.wine.system.empty.description: Install a build from one of the other tabs, or add a folder that contains one.
manage.wine.custom.title: Custom paths
manage.wine.custom.hint: Add folders with Wine or Proton builds that Irori doesn’t find on its own.
manage.wine.custom.prompt: Choose a Wine or Proton folder
manage.onboarding.welcome.title: Welcome to Irori
manage.onboarding.welcome.description: Irori brings your Epic, GOG, Amazon and ZOOM games into one library and runs Windows games with Wine and Proton. A few steps set it up.
manage.onboarding.import.title: Bring over your Heroic setup
manage.onboarding.import.description: Irori found Heroic Games Launcher. Importing keeps your store logins, installed games, per-game settings, favourites and categories. Heroic itself is left unchanged.
manage.onboarding.stores.title: Connect your stores
manage.onboarding.stores.description: Log in to the stores you buy games from. You can skip this and log in later from Accounts.
manage.onboarding.stores.offline: You’re offline. Logging in needs an internet connection.
manage.onboarding.folder.title: Where should games go?
manage.onboarding.folder.description: New installs go into this folder. You can pick another folder for each install, and change this later in Settings.
manage.onboarding.folder.prompt: Choose the folder for new installs
manage.onboarding.done.title: You’re all set
manage.onboarding.done.no_stores: You can log in to stores from Accounts at any time, and add other games from the library.
manage.onboarding.done.stores: Logged in to {stores}. Your games appear in the library as each store finishes loading.
manage.hub.title: Getting started
manage.hub.games.title: Bring in your games
manage.hub.games.description: Log in to your stores, bring games over from other launchers, or add the ROMs already on this computer.
manage.hub.look.title: Make it yours
manage.hub.look.description: Choose how the library shows your games. Changes apply at once, and Settings can change them again.
manage.hub.play.title: While you play
manage.hub.play.description: What Irori can do while a game runs. Turn on the ones you want.
manage.hub.play.overlay: In-game overlay on the controller’s Guide button (beta)
manage.hub.play.replay: Keep a replay buffer to save clips
manage.hub.play.backups: Back up saves with Ludusavi after playing
manage.hub.play.tray: Keep Irori in the tray when its window closes
manage.hub.tips.title: Tips
manage.hub.tips.palette: Press {keys} to find any game or command.
manage.hub.tips.big_picture: Press a controller’s Guide button for Big Picture, made for the couch.
manage.hub.tips.status: Give games a play status, like playing or beaten, to keep track of your backlog.
manage.hub.tips.journal: Write notes about a game on its page; they show on its timeline.
manage.hub.tips.stats: Stats shows where your time went, with a Year in review.

manage.accounts.local_hidden_detail: Its games are left out of your library.

manage.emulators.description: Emulators play games made for consoles and older computers. Install one for each system you want to play; Irori sets it up for you.
manage.emulators.not_downloadable: Irori can’t download {engine} for this computer. Install it from Flathub or your distribution’s software centre and Irori finds it, or choose its program below.
manage.emulators.no_build: {engine} has no version for this computer yet. It runs on {hosts}.
manage.emulators.use_program: Use a program on this computer…
manage.emulators.open.tooltip: Start {engine} without a game, with the settings your games use

manage.rom_sources.looking: Looking in the usual ROM folders…
manage.rom_sources.intro: Irori found games in these folders. Pick the systems to add to your library; nothing is moved or changed.
manage.rom_sources.none: Irori found no ROMs in the usual folders: EmuDeck’s Emulation/roms, RetroDECK’s retrodeck/roms, or a ROMs folder in your home folder or at the top of another disk.
manage.rom_sources.nothing_new: Every system Irori found is already in your library, or no emulator here plays it.
manage.rom_sources.already_one: 1 folder is already in your library.
manage.rom_sources.already_other: {count} folders are already in your library.
manage.rom_sources.unplayable: Games found for systems no emulator here plays: {systems}
manage.rom_sources.added_one: Added 1 ROM folder to your library
manage.rom_sources.added_other: Added {count} ROM folders to your library
manage.rom_sources.found_one: Irori found ROMs for 1 system on this computer.
manage.rom_sources.found_other: Irori found ROMs for {count} systems on this computer.
manage.found.title: Your library is empty
manage.found.description: Here’s what Irori found on this computer. Bring your games in from any of these.
manage.found.steam.signed_in: Signed in as {user}. Your Steam games appear as the library loads.
manage.found.steam.local: Games installed with Steam show up here. Sign in to list your whole Steam library, installed or not.
manage.found.emulation.title: Emulators and ROMs
manage.found.emulation.no_roms: No ROMs in the usual folders.
manage.found.stores.title: Stores
manage.found.stores.description: Log in to the stores you buy games from.
manage.found.loading_hint: Signed-in stores add their games as they finish loading.
manage.emulators.remove_message: Its files are deleted. Games set to use this version will ask you to choose another one.
manage.emulators.custom.description: Use an emulator Irori doesn’t offer, or your own build of one. Irori starts its program with these arguments directly, never through a shell.
manage.emulators.custom.name: Name
manage.emulators.custom.args_help: {rom} stands for the game file; without it, the game goes last. You can also use {placeholders}.
manage.emulators.custom.remove_message: Irori forgets this emulator. Its program stays on this computer, and games that used it play with their system’s default emulator.
manage.emulators.custom.missing: The program of {engine} isn’t there any more. Edit the emulator to choose it again.
manage.emulators.cores.title: Cores · {installed} of {total} installed
manage.emulators.cores.description: RetroArch plays each system with a core. Irori installs the recommended core when you first play a game; you can install others here.
manage.emulators.systems.description: Each system plays with its default emulator unless you choose another one for a game.
manage.emulators.configure.title: {engine} settings
manage.emulators.configure.description: These apply to every game you play with {engine}. You can change them for one game in that game’s settings.
manage.emulators.configure.own_settings_: Irori leaves {engine}’s configuration alone and only tells it where your BIOS files are. Turn this on if you set {engine} up yourself.
manage.engines.option.fullscreen.label: Full screen
manage.engines.option.vsync.label: Vertical sync
manage.engines.option.vsync.help: Matches the frame rate to your display to stop tearing. Turn it off only if games feel slow to respond.
manage.engines.option.show_fps.label: Show frame rate
manage.engines.option.show_fps.help: Shows frames per second in a corner of the screen.
manage.engines.option.video_driver.label: Graphics driver
manage.engines.option.video_driver.help: How the game is drawn. Leave it on Automatic; if a game shows a black screen or crashes at start, try OpenGL.
manage.engines.option.pause_in_backgroun: Pauses the game while you use another window.
manage.engines.option.aspect_ratio.label: Keep the original shape
manage.engines.option.aspect_ratio.help: Shows games in the shape they were made for instead of stretching them to the window.
manage.engines.option.exit_on_quit.label: Close DOSBox when the game quits
manage.engines.option.exit_on_quit.help: Closes DOSBox when the game’s program ends, instead of leaving you at the DOS prompt.
manage.engines.option.widescreen.label: Widescreen
manage.engines.option.widescreen.help: Draws games wider to fill a widescreen display. Some games show glitches at the edges of the picture.
Shows the emulator’s messages, such as saved and loaded states, over the game.
manage.engines.option.boot_logo.label: Show the console’s startup screen
manage.engines.option.boot_logo.help: Starts games through the console’s own startup screen, as on the original. Needs a BIOS file.
manage.emulators.folders.title: Game folders
manage.emulators.folders.description: Irori finds console and retro games in these folders, sorts them by system and adds new ones as they appear.
manage.emulators.bios.title: BIOS files
manage.emulators.bios.description: Some systems need a startup file from your own console, called a BIOS. Irori never downloads them; point it at the folder where you keep yours.
manage.emulators.bios.missing: Needs a BIOS from your console: {files}
manage.emulators.bios.unrecognized: BIOS found but not recognised, it may not work: {files}
manage.setup.title: Set up emulation
manage.setup.folders.intro: Where are your games? Choose the folders that hold your console and retro games; subfolders are included and Irori works out the system of each game.
manage.setup.emulators.intro: Irori recommends one emulator for each system it found. Install them in one go; you can change them later on the Emulators page.
manage.setup.done.title: You’re all set
manage.setup.done.games: {count} games are in your library, ready to play.
manage.setup.done.no_games: Add a folder with games on the Emulators page whenever you’re ready.
manage.onboarding.lutris.description: Irori can bring over your Lutris games (Windows, Linux and emulated), favourites, categories and playtime. Lutris stays as it is.
manage.onboarding.launcher.title: Coming from {launcher}?
manage.onboarding.bottles.description: Irori can add the programs set up in your bottles, each with its bottle as its Wine prefix. Bottles stays as it is.
manage.onboarding.faugus.description: Irori can add your Faugus Launcher games with their prefixes, Proton or Wine builds and launch options. Faugus Launcher stays as it is.
manage.onboarding.playnite.description: Irori can bring over Playnite’s games, art and playtime. Playnite must be closed while it reads; Playnite stays as it is.
manage.launchers.title: Other launchers
manage.launchers.description: Set up third-party launchers in isolated Wine prefixes.
manage.launchers.description_windows: Show games from third-party launchers in your library.
manage.launchers.adopt_prompt: Choose the Wine prefix that has {launcher}
manage.launchers.close_confirm.title: Close {launcher}?
manage.launchers.close_confirm.descripti: “{title}” is running and stops too. Save your game first.
manage.launchers.about.battlenet: Blizzard and Activision games: World of Warcraft, Diablo, Overwatch, Call of Duty.
manage.launchers.about.ea: EA games, including those you own on Steam or Epic that need the EA app.
manage.launchers.about.ubisoft: Ubisoft games, including those that need Ubisoft Connect to start.
manage.launchers.about.rockstar: Grand Theft Auto, Red Dead Redemption and other Rockstar games.
manage.retro.description: Achievements for the games in your ROM folders, matched by RetroAchievements’ hash of each game file.
manage.retro.key_hint: Irori reads your achievements with your username and Web API key. You find the key in the Authentication section of your RetroAchievements settings.
manage.retro.missing: Enter your username and Web API key.
manage.retro.emulators_hint: Sign RetroArch, PCSX2, PPSSPP and Dolphin in with this account so they unlock achievements while you play. Irori uses your password once to get the emulators’ sign-in token and doesn’t keep it.
manage.retro.emulator_enabled: {engine} has achievements turned on. Sign in inside {engine}: it locks its sign-in to this computer, so Irori can’t write it.
manage.retro.hardcore_help: Hardcore unlocks count for more on RetroAchievements; save states, rewinding and cheats are turned off.
manage.retro.no_emulators: No emulator that supports RetroAchievements is installed.
manage.launchers.about.xbox: Microsoft Store and PC Game Pass games.
manage.launchers.xbox.windows_only: Requires Windows to detect Xbox app installs.
manage.friends.title: Friends
manage.friends.invite_hint: To invite friends to a game, start it, open Steam’s friends list and choose “Invite to game” on a friend. Steam offers no other way to invite.
manage.friends.empty: Steam lists no friends for this account.
manage.friends.signed_out: Sign in to Steam in Irori to see your friends.
manage.friends.xbox.signed_out: Sign in to your Xbox account on the Stores page to see your Xbox friends.
manage.friends.xbox.empty: This Xbox account doesn’t follow anyone yet.
manage.friends.xbox.hint: Irori only reads your Xbox friends. Chat with them or invite them in the Xbox app or on your console.
manage.friends.other.intro: Irori lists friends only where a service lets other programs read them.
manage.friends.other.discord: Discord shares friends lists only with apps it has approved for that, and Irori isn’t one. Discord still shows what you play, through Rich Presence.
manage.friends.other.epic: Epic Games keeps its friends service for its own launcher and offers other programs no way to read it.
manage.friends.other.gog: GOG offers no friends API to other programs; your friends stay in GOG Galaxy.
manage.friends.other.launchers: These launchers keep friends inside their own apps, with no way for other programs to read them.
manage.launchers.xbox.account.about: Sync Xbox playtime, achievements and played PC games.
